community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] It's cute, but we had 0 time to actually pay attention to the city we were building. I guess that applies to a lot of city building euros, but here it's even worse. Just accumulate resources and points! It becomes annoyingly fiddly how you have to remember what side of a card you took, and there's slightly more calculation than feels necessary for a game this thin. For no theme anyway. Maybe worse than Point Salad, although not by much.

[Rating: 2/10] Poor copycat of Splendor with terrible, terrible rules and zero theme tie in to the mechanics. Just play Splendor and save your city-building desires for a different game. I can't stress enough: this game is hot garbage. Don't buy into the hype or the cute artwork.

[Rating: 3/10] Simple tableau builder. A very simplified version of Splendor. Resource cards with 2 or more resources have these shown in the corner that is NOT showing when holding them in hand.

[Rating: 3/10] Not my jam. It was fine, but too much like other draft style games. I'd rather play Skyjo.

[Rating: 3/10] An unpleasant game. Annoying to set up, annoying to replenish the tableau, difficult to get a handle on how to win, and goes on for way too long. Splendor is an icon of taut elegance… play that instead.

[Rating: 3/10] Frustrating experience. No catch up mechanic, and a huge luck factor on the display of cards. No recommended.

[Rating: 3/10] Point Salad has more soul, this is too similar to Splendor which is the better game.

[Rating: 4/10] The game goes slower than expected. Refreshing the market delays the game. No clear point targets nor planning.  Points Salad is better! It has faster play, clear planning, and more play and reset feel. We can easily play several games with point salad, but not with this game.
